verdict: Accept as a stylized game-asset prototype; ready for engine wiring. The round-1 majors are fixed or reduced to edge cases (edge-on core signatures, always-on edge lines, raised cell orbit, underside glass, broken material, legal character preset). Weight class reads instantly at every angle and distance tested, tier colour reads to ~25 m, technical validity is excellent and the build is deterministic. One readability gap remains: core identity collapses beyond ~8-10 m and from the side (only Volt survives), so fix it through the far LOD and/or the cells before the look is locked. The rest is polish: degenerate slivers in the heavy bands, left-justified pips, mirror-like Off glass, far-LOD specular pop and some integration notes.

FBX files differ only in embedded timestamps/paths; their re-import matches the glb bounds within 0.5 mm.

issues.issue: Core identity still collapses at in-play distance. At true 1080p pixels it reads at 5 m from the front (Bulwark boxy slab, Mender thin lens, Volt teeth, Phase gap notch). From the side, Mender and Phase are the same plain bar even at 5 m. At 10 m only Volt's teeth survive in silhouette or colour. The spec's idle readability row, a user-decision section, lists the core silhouette at any range.
issues.evidence: review/r2/renders/V01_blind_core_read_5m.png and V01_blind_core_read_10m.png (front/side/back x day/dark/silhouette, cores unlabeled in each row); qa/renders/Q01_distance_read_10_25_50m.png
issues.fix: (a) Far LOD only (seen beyond 20 m, so the near look is unchanged): roughly double the signatures, i.e. Bulwark posts 8.5 to about 18 mm, Volt teeth 30 to about 45 mm, Phase prongs 28 to about 45 mm, Mender ring Z offset 14 to about 28 mm. (b) Code the core into the power cells, which orbit 58 mm above the ring against the sky and are the most visible part at range: ship HALO_PowerCell_<Core> with a distinct silhouette (Bulwark hex prism, Mender twin capsule, Volt spiked crown, Phase open ring). (c) Add a true-pixel 'name the core' blind test at 10 m (front + side) to the standard renders and iterate until at least 3 of the 4 cores can be named.

issues.issue: All Heavy bands contain zero-area sliver triangles (collinear verts on the slab outer face): Bulwark 8, Mender 18, Volt 18, Phase 17 in the exported glb. They make Blender's Wireframe modifier throw vertices out to about 900 m, and they will break tangent generation, outline shells or any mesh processing. The kit QA does not test for them, so NOTES' '0 problems' misses them.
issues.evidence: review/r2/r2_glb_report.json (degenerate_tris on the Band_Heavy graphite primitive); r2_checks_report.json zero_area_at, e.g. Bulwark (0.2334, 0.0143, -0.0132) and Volt (-0.0585, -0.2039, -0.0147) Blender coordinates
issues.fix: In halo_parts.band_heavy (face_d slab profile), drop the near-collinear profile vertex, or run bmesh.ops.dissolve_degenerate(dist=1e-5) in MB.finish. Add a zero-area triangle check (area < 1e-10) to qa/qa_glb.py.

issues.issue: The tier pips are left-justified. The engine shows PIP_1..PIP_n with PIP_1 at x = -24 mm, so a T1 halo's single pip sits 24 mm left of the front centre and the T2/T3 groups are off-centre too. On the Volt (and other cores seen slightly from above), the lower half of each pip merges into the same-coloured lit glass behind it, so the pips read as triangles.
issues.evidence: review/r2/renders/V03_closeups.png (top: Bulwark/Volt T1 and T2 front views); renders/04_character_fullbody_idle.png (3 pips left of centre); renders/02c_weight_eyelevel_idle.png (Light pip off-centre)
issues.fix: Use a centred layout per count, x_i = (i - (n + 1) / 2) * 16 mm. Either ship empties per count (HALO_<Core>_PIP_<n>_<i>) or ship one centre empty and document the formula, then update place_halo and NOTES. Put a small graphite backing plate behind the pip row on the Volt, Mender and Phase Head arcs.

issues.issue: M_HALO_Glass_Off is almost a mirror (roughness 0.08, clearcoat 1.0, specular 0.8). Uncovered and broken arcs throw white highlights (Volt teeth, Bulwark wall) that at range read like T1 white glass, so an uncovered arc can be mistaken for covered.
issues.evidence: review/r2/renders/V03_closeups.png (seam panels: the uncovered Arms glass shows a white sheen); V05_arc_states_ingame.png (the uncovered Volt Head arc has 12 near-white pixels at 5 m, the lit one has 16)
issues.fix: Change Glass_Off to roughness 0.3-0.35, clearcoat 0.3 and specular 0.5, keeping it dark. Verify in Bevy under the map's environment light.

issues.issue: The far LOD pops brighter at the 20 m switch. Its frame is one smooth chamfered sweep that catches broad specular and blooms to white pixels, which are the brightest pixels on the halo (Bulwark Medium/Heavy). This risks a T1 misread and makes the LOD swap visible. NOTES lists it as a known limitation but understates it.
issues.evidence: review/r2/renders/V07_far_lod_switch.png (near rows vs far rows at 20 m, true pixels); renders/07_far_lod.png (far frames read light silver, near frames dark graphite)
issues.fix: Give the far frame a rougher graphite (about 0.8; e.g. M_HALO_Graphite_Far) and mark its chamfer edges sharp so highlights stay narrow. Re-check at 20 m against the near kit until mean luminance matches within about 10 %.

issues.issue: Back power cells still hide at close range. At -10 deg (viewer about 1.8 m away), a Heavy halo shows its true 3 cells only 33-47 % of the orbit, and a Light halo shows 0 cells 11-23 % of the orbit.
issues.evidence: review/r2/r2_cell_visibility_report.json (ring + band + cell-on-cell occlusion); NOTES.md acknowledges 38-50 %
issues.fix: Use a per-weight orbit height (Light 0.058, Medium 0.065, Heavy 0.080), or stagger the cells vertically by ±10-12 mm in phase, so far-side cells clear the front band. Weight still reads from size at 2 m, so this is low priority.

issues.issue: Facing gotcha for Bevy. The halo glTF faces +Z (Head arc +Z, Arms +X), but the game's player entity faces -Z (render.rs arc_angle puts Head at -Z and Arms at -X, the player's left). NOTES says the halo needs 'no extra rotation', which is only true relative to the character file. If the halo copies the gameplay yaw directly, the Head arc ends up behind the player and Arms on the right.
issues.evidence: game/crates/val_etf/src/render.rs arc_angle(); export/HALO_*.glb Arc_Head bbox at +Z (r2_glb_report.json); NOTES.md 'Axes and attachment'
issues.fix: In NOTES, state explicitly: rotate the halo root 180 deg about Y in Bevy (the same fix-up as the character glTF) so that HALO_*_Arc_Head points along the player's forward (-Z). Add a one-line check: the Head arc faces the camera when the player faces the camera.

issues.issue: Each per-core glb is a flat pile of 17 root nodes in which the near arcs, both band weights, the far glass and all three far frames overlap at the origin. Spawning HALO_<Core>.glb#Scene0 renders every LOD and both bands at once. NOTES' primitive table also says bands are 'graphite, gunmetal, lip glass, edge', but every Medium band has no gunmetal primitive, so its lip glass is primitive 1.
issues.evidence: review/r2/r2_glb_report.json (scene_roots = 17; Band_Medium primitives: Graphite, Glass_T1, Edge)
issues.fix: Parent the nodes under empties HALO_<Core>_Near, HALO_<Core>_Bands and HALO_<Core>_Far, or export the far set to HALO_<Core>_Far.glb, so the engine can toggle a whole group. Correct the primitive table and require lookup by material name only.

issues.issue: Draw calls and triangles per halo are still high. A Heavy halo has about 26 primitives (4 arcs x 3, band x 4, 3 cells x 2, up to 4 pips) and about 7.9k triangles. HALO_PowerCell alone is 488 tris, mostly dense dome caps, and three of them orbit every Heavy halo.
issues.fix: Merge the static graphite + edge parts of the 4 arcs and the band into one frame mesh per core x weight (2 primitives), leaving only the 4 arc-glass primitives (plus lip) swappable, for about 8 draws per halo. Cut the cell caps to 8-sided low domes (about 150 tris per cell).

issues.issue: build_halo.py hard-codes HERE = r'F:/git/val etf/assets/shields', and halo_render.py hard-codes CHAR_GLB, so the build only runs from that exact checkout. halo_data, make_sprites and make_catalog already resolve paths from __file__.
issues.evidence: build_halo.py line 27; halo_render.py line 19; the reviewer's sandbox rebuild needed a patched copy
issues.fix: Set HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)) and resolve CHAR_GLB relative to the repo root (HERE/../characters/kestrel/trellis/...).
